dedupe_keys.name: the largest crop production shocks of every country 1961 to 2023 magnitude causes and frequency

description: This case study finds the largest crop production shock in every country from FAO crop production data for 1961 to 2023 and identifies its causes, to highlight major risks to the food system. The authors, from research groups working on global catastrophic risk and Earth system resilience, published it as an open-access journal article. They measured each country's largest year-on-year drop in production and classified causes as climate, economic disruption, environmental hazards such as storms, or conflict, then computed how often shocks of given size occur at country, continent and global level. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: FAO statistics vary in quality between countries and years, cause attribution relies on documentary evidence, and production shocks do not measure food access directly. The study shows that large crop production shocks happen regularly in all countries, most often driven by drought; the global mean of the largest country shocks was a 29 percent drop, with African countries hit hardest (80 percent in Botswana); global shocks above 5 percent occur about once in 63 years, while continent-level shocks of that size occur every 1.8 years. Simulation uses: setting the size and frequency of production shock scenarios in food supply network and cascade models. Related records: FAOSTAT (data-faostat) is the underlying data and the food shocks cascade model (model-food-shocks-cascade-fsc) propagates such shocks through trade.
